/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 08 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2973 (-21)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4512 (-85)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2410 (26)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1808 (8)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1000 (-3)
CAPESIZE
The BCI 182 5TC fell by $768 to $40,923 today, with the Atlantic continuing to soften while the Pacific remained relatively well supported. The C5 index edged up 0.130 to $14.725, while C3 slipped 0.935 to $33.725. The Pacific has seen an exceptionally busy week in terms of miner volume and fixture activity, although the market's reaction has arguably been less pronounced than the level of activity might suggest. With the tonnage list now considerably shorter, some support emerged today. Two C5 miners were active, with offers reportedly starting the day around $16 before talk circulated of $15.50 being offered to a miner, who ultimately fixed several vessels around $14.70. A Newcastlemax was also reported fixed by another miner at $14.55. The South Brazil and West Africa to China market continued to ease following several fixtures concluded yesterday in the low $34s on C3. Offers today were heard around $34.50, with a noticeable lack of bids, although activity remained relatively subdued despite brokers reporting an increase in enquiry.
PANAMAX
Activity across both basins improved notably today, with the P5TC rising by $232 to $21,688. Market sources reported increased trans-Atlantic mineral demand, which is helping to support both P1A levels and overall sentiment. Offers are said to be moving higher, while the fixing floor has also continued to strengthen, reflecting firmer market fundamentals. The North Atlantic has been singled out as a particularly active region, with increased fixing activity helping to reinforce the positive tone across the basin. Today has seen a marked increase in reported trans-Atlantic East Coast South America fixtures, reflecting the stronger activity levels seen over recent days. Fronthaul business from the region is once again being described as highly laycan dependent, with tonnage for October loading reported to be tightening. By contrast, more forward positions are said to be attracting a wider bid-offer spread, highlighting the differing sentiment between prompt and forward dates. The Chorus (82,181 2011) open Wilhelmshaven 9 October was said to have been placed on subjects for a US East Coast to the Continent with Arcelormittal, although no other details surfaced. ADM were said to have placed the AP Dubrovnik (82,249 2023) Hazira 13 October on subjects for an EC South America fronthaul at $25,850. Similar business was reportedly concluded on subjects by both the Agia Valentini (80,458 2012) Abidjan prompt and the Atalandi (77,528 2014) Paradip 26 September, although no other details surfaced. Activity in the Pacific is said to be gaining momentum once again, with both the North Pacific and Australia leading the increase in demand. Market participants have also noted that the potential for weather-related delays in the North Pacific is influencing chartering decisions, with charterers reportedly willing to pay a premium for tonnage that can offer greater certainty over arrival dates and loading schedules.
SUPRAMAX
Another similar day in line with the rest of the week. Despite the disruption of holidays in the East, the market there has seen a slow increase throughout the week, and the round voyage rate again carried the Index today with the 11TC average was up $93 to close at $22,851. The south Atlantic has seen more activity as rates eased slightly, the US Gulf seemed very positional with fronthaul rates softening more than the transatlantic bids and the Continent continues to outperform the rest of the Atlantic. There were higher rates again reported in the North Pacific with NoPac grains continuing their rise, supported by reasonable backhaul activity and steady demand in South East Asia.

Atlantic
The Atlas (63,496 2017) went on subjects basis delivery Santos about 21 October for a trip South Korea intention agriprods at $19,250 plus $925,000 ballast bonus to Polaris and the Pac Alcamar (63,000 2021) fixed when/where ready San Lorenzo for a trip Vietnam with agriprods at $19,500 plus $950,000 ballast bonus with Cargill. The Abu Al Abyad (57,369 2011) open Dakar 10 October fixed a voyage grains stem from River Plate to Iraq with TAF, but the rate remained private with brokers suggesting the timecharter equivalent was around $24,000 plus $1,400,000 ballast bonus basis delivery Recalada, and the Globe Cleopatra (58,765 2009) open Altamira was on subjects basis delivery US Gulf trip China with petcoke at $30,000 with Aries Bulk.

Asia
The Metis Titanium (61,050 2021) prompt in North China was reportedly on subjects to Canpotex for a NoPac round voyage at $25,000 and the Oriente Gloria (61,425 2013) Port Qasim 12-14 October went on subjects to Lucky Cement at $27,500 plus $275,000 ballast bonus delivery Richards Bay for a trip back to Pakistan/WC India.
HANDYSIZE
It was a mixed day of activity, with movements ranging from minor to more pronounced across both basins. The BHSI fell by 3 points to 1,000, while the 7TC average declined by $52 to close at $18,004. In the Continent and Mediterranean, activity remained subdued and sentiment was largely positional, with rates holding broadly in line with previous fixtures and little fresh direction emerging. The South Atlantic, however, continued to see fresh demand and healthy activity, with rates reflecting a firmer tone. In contrast, the US Gulf continued to lag, as ample tonnage and limited fresh demand maintained downward pressure on rates. Across Asia, the market remained well balanced, with a few additional fixtures reported and rates trending largely flat.

Market Fundamentals
Fortescue Q3 Results

In the quarter ending September 2026, Fortescue (FMG) reported preliminary iron ore shipments 2.9 Mt lower than the same period last year at 46.8 Mt. During the quarter, shipments were affected by maintenance, including scheduled port outload shutdown activity. Iron ore sales of 42.9 Mt came in below shipments of 46.8 Mt during the period, representing the impact of ongoing negotiations with China’s state iron ore buyer, China Mineral Resources Group (CMRG).
